subject: Myth & Symbolism
subcategory: The World Tree and Cosmic Maps
title: West the Land of the Dead
description: One-minute skill: West the Land of the Dead.

hook.text: The sun sets in the west. Egyptians placed the afterlife there. The dead go where the sun dies.

buildup.text: Egyptian tombs are on the Nile's west bank. The living stayed east. The river divided life from death.

discovery.text: Celtic myth placed the Otherworld on western islands—Tír na nÓg, the Land of the Young, beyond the setting sun.

twist.text: Tolkien's Valinor is in the West. Frodo sails west at the end. He borrowed the Celtic pattern: death is westward.

climax.text: West is where things end: the day, the journey, the story. Going west means leaving the land of the living.

punchline.text: Follow the sun. It leads to the end.

quiz.question: Why did Egyptians build tombs on the west bank of the Nile?
options: The sun sets in the west, linking it to death
